author: PavelMakarchuk
body:
**Verdict: Question — no action needed.**

Components below are for the record currently in `out2psl/1085` (`taxsimid 2714813`: ID, MFJ, ages 65/68, 43,434 intrec / 38,458 pensions / 24,945 gssi). Note it differs from this issue's title case (IA 58/57, 104K wages) — the bundled Iowa 1040 PDF matches the title case, while the 39R/40 PDFs match this one.

| PE (current, queried) | |
|---|---|
| Fed AGI (v10) | 103,094.51 = 43,433.84 interest + 38,457.52 pensions + 21,203.15 taxable SS (85%) |
| 39R Part B subtractions | 21,203 (SS only; line 8 retirement benefits deduction = 0) |
| ID std deduction (v34) | 27,800 = 25,100 + 2 × 1,350 (both spouses 65+) |
| ID taxable (v36) / tax | 54,091.36; tax 3,030.08 − 240 grocery credit → siitax 2,790.08 |

PE computes 39R line 8 in [`id_retirement_benefits_deduction`](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/blob/master/policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/id/tax/income/deductions/retirement_benefits/id_retirement_benefits_deduction.py) but limits qualifying income to [public pensions + military retirement](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/blob/master/policyengine_us/parameters/gov/states/id/tax/income/deductions/retirement_benefits/income_sources.yaml) per [Idaho Code §63-3022A](https://legislature.idaho.gov/statutesrules/idstat/title63/t63ch30/sect63-3022a/) (CSRS, Idaho police/firefighter, military), so a generic TAXSIM `pensions` amount gets $0 — matching your unchecked-box 39R (8f = 0). The "qualified" TA run instead deducts 8f = min(56,664 − 24,944 SS, 38,457) = 31,720; should the box be unchecked for a generic pension? Separately, TA's std deduction 26,450 (one $1,350 add-on) and grocery credit 220 suggest it treated one spouse as under 65 — with input ages 65/68 both qualify, which is the remaining $1,350 of the PE-vs-TA taxable-income gap.
